correctness.rationale: The first-bit-plus-derivative representation is bijective, a repetition inserts one derivative zero, and fixed-weight zero-bin descendant intersection is exactly characterized by \(\ell_1\)-distance. This yields the six layer optima \((1,2,3,1,1,1)\) and equality counts \((1,3,1,10,5,1)\). The standalone verifier independently reconstructs direct one- and two-repetition descendant sets for all \(64\) words, checks the bin criterion on every relevant pair, exhaustively enumerates every layer subset, constructs all \(150\) sector maxima, and checks coverage.

value.rationale: The result closes a natural finite extremal instance in the foundational repetition-error model, at the first length where the derivative-weight-two layer supports three mutually compatible representatives. It supplies a complete equality classification and exact descendant-space coverage, exposing rigid finite structure not furnished by the cited asymptotic constructions. The result is therefore more than a routine recomputation of a known optimum.
